what: Ground truth for the reference pacing measurement. Each row is one minute of one reference, read off a 1 fps contact sheet and counted by eye.
why: The automatic cut detector could not be trusted across these six references. Calibrated on one LEMMiNO minute it read 18 against a hand count of 18, and on another minute of the same film it read 1 against 7. On footage-led material it over-reads instead: 19 against 8. The error is not noise, it is a property of the material — a detector fires inside a moving shot and stays quiet between two photographs that share a palette. So the absolute numbers in reference_pacing.md come from these rows, and the detector supplies the shape of the curve between them.

method.sheet: ffmpeg fps=1, scale=320, tile=10x6 — sixty frames, one per second
method.counted: distinct shots visible in the minute
method.a_shot: one continuous camera or graphic take. A reveal inside a held graphic, an annotation appearing over a diagram, or a push across one still is NOT a new shot.
method.known_bias: a shot shorter than one second can fall between two sampled frames and be missed, so these counts are a slight under-count of the fastest passages
